Archie vs Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark and Grok Bot.

The AI companies now sell agents too, and they make the same promise we do. This is the comparison where the difference is genuinely one thing: whose computer the agent works on.

Archie is in testing and not for sale yet. See where it stands → Checked against the sources below on August 20, 2026.

The short answer

Same promise. Different computer.

All four of these run tasks while you are away, hold work for your approval, and message you when something is done. The difference is where. Cowork’s sessions run on Anthropic’s serversSource 2, Spark works with your phone and laptop off because it runs on Google’sSource 3, and each Grok Bot gets a computer of its own in xAI’s cloudSource 4. Archie runs on the computer you own, which is a real limitation and the entire point.

A cloud agent suits you if

  • You want it working with every computer you own switched off
  • You already pay the subscription it comes bundled with
  • You live inside one company’s apps and like it there
  • You want something you can use today

Archie suits you if

  • You want your files, sessions and history kept on your computer
  • You want the credentials it uses held in your computer’s password store, not on someone’s VM
  • You want to pick the AI company, and change your mind later
  • You want an approval gate that has no off switch
Side by side

One difference, and everything it drags with it.

Archie compared with Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark and Grok Bot, across where the agent runs, where your content and credentials live, which AI answers, approvals, and cost

Claude prices read from Anthropic’s own pricing page on August 20, 2026. Spark and Grok Bot are deliberately left unpriced: Google renders its plan prices per region, and xAI’s pricing sits behind pages we could not read at source, so their tiers are named without figures rather than guessed.

Where they win

Four things their cloud buys.

This is the strongest competition Archie has, and pretending otherwise would tell you something about every other page on this site.

No computer of yours stays on

Their agent works from a computer they run, so yours can be shut, lost, or at the bottom of a bag. Archie stops when your computer does, and that is not a footnote.

You may already be paying for one

Cowork is included on the Claude plan a lot of people already have. An agent for zero additional dollars is a serious argument, and $30 a month plus usage has to earn its difference.

Their own apps, deeply

Spark inside Gmail, Calendar and Drive is the home team playing at home. Archie connects to those from outside, and outside is outside.

You can try them now

All three are shipping, in beta or generally available. Archie is in testing and not for sale yet, and this page does not get to pretend that away.

Worth saying

Same models. That is not a coincidence.

Anthropic, Google and xAI are 3 of the 7 companies Archie connects to, so the intelligence on both sides of this page is literally the same. What the biggest AI companies building agents proves is that the category is real. What it cannot change is the shape of the deal: their agent lives with them, and yours lives with you. If custody is not a thing you care about, they are excellent products. This whole site is for the people who care.

Sources for every figure and claim on this page
1Claude Cowork, on paid Claude plans

Anthropic’s pricing page, claude.com/pricing, lists “Includes Claude Cowork” on the Pro card, $20 a month or $17 billed annually, read on August 20, 2026. The permission modes, including Skip (“Claude doesn’t pause to ask and nothing checks its actions automatically”), are in Anthropic’s own guide.

2Where Cowork runs

“Claude’s work runs on Anthropic’s servers, in an isolated environment, and your sessions and files are saved to your Claude account.” From Anthropic’s getting-started guide, read on August 20, 2026.

3Gemini Spark

“Works in the background 24/7, even if your phone and laptop are turned off,” for Google AI Ultra subscribers in select countries, with app connections off by default and the agent “designed to check with you before taking major actions”. From Google’s own Spark page, read on August 20, 2026.

4Grok Bot

In beta for SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra and Cursor Teams Premium, on desktop and iOS; each Bot “runs on a persistent cloud VM with a browser, filesystem, and terminal” and comes back “when something needs your approval”. From xAI’s announcement and its documentation, read on August 20, 2026.

5Archie’s side of the table

The custody claim, the 7 providers, and the approval gate that cannot be turned off are all on our Trust page, each pointing at the code that makes it true, with instructions for watching the traffic yourself.

6Archie, $30 a month

Our own price, with the AI usage that sits on top of it broken down on the pricing page.

What we have not claimed

Nothing here says these products are careless with your content: all three companies document isolation, defaults and approvals, and we quote them doing it. The claim is only that their agent works on their computer and Archie works on yours, and that the difference matters to some people. Each company’s own security documentation is the place to judge their side properly.
